name: Dreamoon Likes Sequences
description: Dreamoon likes sequences very much. So he created a problem about the sequence that you can't find in OEIS: You are given two integers $$$d, m$$$, find the number of arrays $$$a$$$, satisfying the following constraints: The length of $$$a$$$ is $$$n$$$, $$$n \ge 1$$$ $$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \dots \lt a_n \le d$$$ Define an array $$$b$$$ of length $$$n$$$ as follows: $$$b_1 = a_1$$$, $$$\forall i \gt 1, b_i = b_{i - 1} \oplus a_i$$$, where $$$\oplus$$$ is the bitwise exclusive-or (xor). After constructing an array $$$b$$$, the constraint $$$b_1 \lt b_2 \lt \dots \lt b_{n - 1} \lt b_n$$$ should hold. Since the number of possible arrays may be too large, you need to find the answer modulo $$$m$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 100$$$) denoting the number of test cases in the input. Each of the next $$$t$$$ lines contains two integers $$$d, m$$$ ($$$1 \leq d, m \leq 10^9$$$). Note that $$$m$$$ is not necessary the prime!
output_specification: For each test case, print the number of arrays $$$a$$$, satisfying all given constrains, modulo $$$m$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1329B — Dreamoon Likes Sequences [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
